segments.title: Chương 194: Bước đầu của Weibo
segments.content:
Chapter 197: Weibo Takes Its First Step. October 18th.

CCTV-6, the movie channel, launched in Hong Kong, making it available to Hong Kong residents from now on.

At the celebratory banquet, stars from mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan were all invited to offer their congratulations.

To the astonishment of a crowd of entertainment industry heavyweights, Jane Zhang attended the banquet as a guest and performed a song.

At the same time, CCTV-6 announced on the spot that Jane Zhang would soon be starring in *Song of the Movies*, and moreover, she would be in every performance—a very significant role!

The media reporters and some of the stars present were stunned.

*Song of the Movies* was a musical commemorating the 100th anniversary of Chinese cinema, directed by Golden Horse Award-winning director Mabel Cheung, with Jonathan Lee serving as the musical director for the entire production. A host of stars were set to perform, and even Jackie Chan had managed to shoehorn his son into the cast.

Rehearsals and ticket sales were about to begin, and suddenly they were bringing in a Super Girl for a major role?

Jane Zhang, whose popularity had been waning, was once again the subject of frenzied reports by major media outlets, immediately followed by the news that she had signed with Huayi Brothers.

Then, a group photo from a "Star Jelly" dinner party was revealed.

Huang Jianxiang, Angus Tung, Chen Daoming (former director of Sony Music), Hei Nan (a top-tier music producer), Zeng Zimo (a Phoenix TV host), Cheng Qingsong (a director and screenwriter)... all claimed to be fans of Jane Zhang and had dinner together.

Along with a few bosses from Chengdu, they established the Jane Zhang Global Fan Club.

The vast majority of people couldn't understand why Jane Zhang had such a deep network of connections.

It was actually very simple. Before participating in Super Girl, Jane Zhang had been a resident singer at the Music House in Chengdu for three years. Many wealthy and famous people frequented that place!

One of the Music House's shareholders, nicknamed "Iron Hoop Roller," and an IT company boss known as "Old Wang of Chengdu" were the behind-the-scenes movers who helped Jane Zhang build her network.

And Jane Zhang's boyfriend, Feng Ke, was just a minor figure running errands at this time.

Without pressure from these people, would EE-Media have willingly let Jane Zhang terminate her contract?

Interestingly, it seemed those two behind-the-scenes figures were genuinely just helping out.

They didn't interfere with Jane Zhang's management contract, nor did they help her secure commercial collaborations. Apart from occasionally inviting Jane Zhang back to the Music House to sing, they didn't seem to gain any benefits.

When Chen Guiliang hired Jane Zhang for an endorsement at a low price, neither of them stepped in to stop it.

Huayi, who had signed Jane Zhang's record deal, was currently promoting her frantically, even planning to send her to perform on Broadway in the United States.

To be honest, seeing this kind of momentum, Chen Guiliang was also a bit bewildered.

He truly hadn't expected to have signed everyone's darling.

Just as Jane Zhang's popularity reached its peak, her commercial for Kaixin001 was released.

"Old Wang of Chengdu" might not have been surnamed Wang; his identity had always been a mystery.

There were only two confirmed pieces of information: first, he was the boss of an IT company; second, he had personally contacted the boss of Huayi Brothers to arrange Jane Zhang's contract.

He was now the head of the Chengdu branch of Jane Zhang's global fan club.

This fan club was very formal and organized, even properly registered with the Civil Affairs Bureau. It also had its own articles of association, the two most important of which were: not to go against Jane Zhang's personal wishes, and not to interfere with Jane Zhang's management affairs.

"Old Wang of Chengdu" sent a message in the fan group: "Tonight at 8 PM, Jane's first solo endorsement commercial will go live on online platforms like Tudou and Sohu Video."

"Roger!"

"Always Jane."

"Why is it such a minor endorsement? It's not even on TV."

"She shouldn't have taken this kind of deal."

"I heard EE-Media intentionally signed it for a low price just to spite Jane."

"I think we should boycott it!"

Seeing negative comments in the fan group, "Old Wang of Chengdu" typed a reminder: "Article Two of the fan club charter: Fans shall not interfere with Jane's management affairs."

"Alright, I won't boycott it then."

"I hope the commercial is well-made."

"Kaixin001 isn't bad. Ever since Jane registered an account on Kaixin001, I've become a user too."

"You fake fans, haven't you even followed Jane on Kaixin001 yet?"

It wasn't just the fans in Chengdu who took action; fans from other regions also mobilized, proactively helping to post everywhere—their goal was surprisingly to get people to watch Jane Zhang's commercial.

This group's ability to mobilize was astounding; whenever they took action, their call was met with a massive response.

By the end of this year, through the fan club's meticulous planning and collective action, Jane Zhang would surpass all other stars from the mainland, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, becoming Yahoo Search's "Hottest Singer of the Year" and the overall champion of NetEase's "China Idol · 2005 Online Popularity King" poll.

Rational, yet fanatical.

Tan Yutong was a member of the fan club. A graduate of Zhejiang University's computer science department, he was a standard-issue tech guy, now working as a programmer at a foreign company.

He had never chased after stars before. It was only because he once said, "Among the Super Girls, Jane Zhang's singing is the best" during an argument on the Tianya forum. Soon after, someone contacted him, inviting him to join the fan club and presenting him with the charter and fan benefits.

Tan Yutong joined in a daze, and then he found the group to be amazing; everyone was like brothers and sisters.

After receiving the message in the fan group, Tan Yutong, on a whim, actually sat waiting in front of his computer for Jane Zhang's commercial to be released.

When the time came, Tan Yutong repeatedly refreshed the webpage.

After a delay of about a minute, the full commercial finally appeared on Tudou's homepage.

Chen Guiliang had produced two versions.

One version was a 15-second spot attached to other videos, mainly used on sites like Sohu Video because users on these sites couldn't upload their own content, and the advertising fees were particularly expensive.

The other version was a full three minutes long!

Tan Yutong clicked on the three-minute full version on the homepage, which buffered for a while before he could watch it.

The screen was initially dim, with the sound of footsteps approaching from a distance. A woman slowly walked out, visible only as a silhouette, highlighting a graceful and sexy figure.

Along with the sound effects, lights came on one by one.

Tan Yutong's eyes widened; he had never seen such a beautiful Jane Zhang. Her skin was fairer, her figure better, and every move exuded an elegant charm.

This look was created by Mao Geping's team. Including the rental of the evening gown and jewelry, Chen Guiliang had spent a full 150,000 yuan!

The scene suddenly flashed back. Jane Zhang became ordinary, working in a restaurant. Then singing in a bar, returning listlessly to her rented room at night. Then came the Super Girl auditions...

During the competition, she was physically and mentally exhausted. She stumbled upon Kaixin001 and registered an account.

From zero followers, her fan count gradually grew to ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand... After every competition, whether excited or aggrieved, she would share it on Kaixin001.

Interspersed in the video were fans from all walks of life, sharing the idol's joys and sorrows through Kaixin001.

Then, Jane Zhang activated the Weibo feature. Standing on a street corner, she took a selfie with her phone and casually sent out a Weibo post with the photo.

Fans from all professions—some at work, some eating, some riding the bus—all received Jane Zhang's text and multimedia messages.

The scene cut back to Jane Zhang in her evening gown, picking up a microphone and starting to sing.

A voiceover said: "Mobile Weibo, your idol right by your side!"

Tan Yutong was quite surprised. There was actually a feature like this.

He had a Kaixin001 account, having been dragged into it by other fans, and had only followed Jane Zhang at first. He knew about Weibo but couldn't be bothered to learn about its specific functions.

In the comment section below the video, many fans had already left comments.

"Wow, Jane is so beautiful in this commercial!"

"Kaixin001 spent a sky-high price of 150,000 yuan to hire a top team to create Jane's look." (This was a paid comment)

"Kaixin001 is so sincere." (This was a paid comment)

"This Weibo feature is really interesting, it's like Jane is sending us text messages." (This was a paid comment)

"I just read Jane's Kaixin001 journal entry. She said she was very happy with this collaboration and will officially post her first Weibo at nine tonight." (This was a paid comment)

"How much does it cost to activate the Weibo feature? I can't afford it if it's expensive."

"Receiving text messages is 8 yuan a month. Receiving MMS is 12 yuan a month. You can choose just one. Here's how to do it..." (This was a paid comment)

"A bit expensive, I'm a student."

"This commercial is very inspirational. It shows all of Jane's hardships along the way."

"Jane."

Xie Yang had also sent people to infiltrate Jane Zhang's various fan groups. At this moment, they were sending messages in the groups: "Jane, I just activated the Weibo feature. I'll be able to receive Jane's texts from now on!"

"Jane's follower count on Kaixin001 is only a little over 30,000? She's being surpassed by everyone else! For those who don't have a Kaixin001 account yet, you can go register one. Let's make Jane's follower count number one on the whole site!"

With just a few simple words, many fans became fired up, swarming to Kaixin001 to register accounts.

These were the people who could make Jane Zhang Yahoo Search's Hottest Singer of the Year and NetEase's China Idol Online Popularity King. Their incredible ability to mobilize was no joke.

And they didn't just go themselves; they pulled other fans along with them.

In just one night, Jane Zhang's follower count on Kaixin001 surged by more than six thousand, with most of them being newly registered accounts. And this was only the beginning.
